Noty my idea originally but been thinking about this framing...

China shock 1.0: cheap goods. After joining the WTO in December 2001, China took on the world's low-end manufacturing and became the factory for ordinary goods. Toys, textiles, furniture, electronics assembly. Economists later put the cost at over 2 million lost US manufacturing jobs. The consumer-facing version of this is what everyone knows: Alibaba connecting Western buyers to Chinese factories, then Shein and Temu shipping the factory floor straight to your doorstep. Cheap, everywhere, unbeatable on price.

China shock 2.0: high-end manufacturing. This ramped up through the late 2010s and accelerated hard after COVID. China stopped just making cheap versions of things and started making the best versions. In 2023 it passed Japan as the world's largest car exporter, and BYD outsold Volkswagen inside China, VW's biggest market for decades. Add CATL in batteries, an 80%+ grip on the solar supply chain, half of global shipbuilding, DJI owning drones. The old high-end hubs are feeling it. German industry, built on combustion-engine excellence, is closing plants at home for the first time in VW's history. These products aren't as good as the incumbents'. They're often better, and cheaper.

China shock 3.0: robots. This is the one coming, and it will be bigger than the first two combined. The humanoid and robotics wave isn't one industry, it's a bid on the entire physical economy: factories, warehouses, logistics, eventually homes. And China is uniquely positioned to supply it. Chinese firms shipped 97% of the world's humanoid robots in the first half of 2026. Unitree and AgiBot alone control roughly three quarters of the market, and Unitree just went public in Shanghai with a first day pop over 400%. This isn't luck. It's the direct payoff of shocks 1.0 and 2.0: the EV supply chain (batteries, motors, sensors, actuators) is basically the humanoid supply chain, and it all sits within a two-hour drive in the Yangtze Delta. Beijing has made it explicit national policy, targeting 100,000 deployed humanoids by 2027.

They have the power, the robots and even the AI models. It's hard to bet against China.

effective_posts.translation_zh:
原本不是我的想法，但一直在思考这个框架……

中国冲击 1.0：廉价商品。2001 年 12 月加入 WTO 后，中国承接了世界的低端制造业，成为普通商品的工厂。玩具、纺织品、家具、电子产品组装。后来经济学家估算，其代价是美国制造业流失了超过 200 万个工作岗位。面向消费者的版本就是大家都知道的：Alibaba 将西方买家与中国工厂连接起来，然后 Shein 和 Temu 把工厂车间直接送到你家门口。便宜、无处不在、价格无敌。

中国冲击 2.0：高端制造业。这在 2010 年代末期逐步加速，并在 COVID 之后急剧提速。中国不再只是制造廉价版本的东西，而是开始制造最好的版本。2023 年，中国超过日本成为全球最大的汽车出口国，而 BYD 在中国国内的销量超过了 Volkswagen——中国是 VW 数十年来最大的市场。再加上电池领域的 CATL、对太阳能供应链 80% 以上的掌控、全球一半的造船量、DJI 主导无人机。老牌高端中心正在感受到冲击。以燃油发动机卓越技术为基础的德国工业，正在 VW 历史上首次关闭本土工厂。这些产品并不是和既有厂商的一样好。它们往往更好，而且更便宜。

中国冲击 3.0：机器人。这是即将到来的冲击，而且会比前两次加起来还要大。人形机器人和机器人浪潮不是一个行业，而是对整个实体经济的押注：工厂、仓库、物流，最终还有家庭。而中国在供应这方面处于独特位置。2026 年上半年，中国企业出货了全球 97% 的人形机器人。仅 Unitree 和 AgiBot 就控制了大约四分之三的市场，而 Unitree 刚刚在上海上市，首日涨幅超过 400%。这不是运气。这是冲击 1.0 和 2.0 的直接回报：EV 供应链（电池、电机、传感器、执行器）基本上就是人形机器人的供应链，而且这一切都位于长三角两小时车程范围内。北京已将其明确列为国家政策，目标是到 2027 年部署 100,000 台人形机器人。

他们有电力、机器人，甚至还有 AI 模型。很难押注反对中国。

Zwei mutige Leute wollten ihn stoppen, andere sahen zu. Ein ganzer Kreis von Menschen bildete sich um das Geschehen. Es gab eine Schlägerei, letztendlich kam die Security dazu und es brauchte 6!! Leute um den Dieb zu Boden zu bringen. 
Unglaublich 😡!
Ich denke, bei den kommenden Inventuren wird da einiges nicht passen 😉.

我女儿昨天又去了慕尼黑。她得以现场观察了一下“城市景象”。在 Saturn，有个“金贵货”抱着一个大 x-box 纸箱直接往外走，出口处的报警器响了😳。
两个勇敢的人想拦住他，其他人在旁边看。一整圈人围着这件事。发生了斗殴，最后保安来了，需要 6!! 个人才把这个小偷按倒在地。
难以置信😡！
我想，接下来的盘点会有不少对不上的地方😉。
